Stryker._comment: Bangalore site (not 'Stryker NCR', which is a separate client). Its theme_map is empty, so the default weekday themes apply and Tuesday is the Chinese day.

rules._comment: Chinese Tuesday serves a north or south Indian veg dry, whichever suits that day's menu.
rules.name: theme_cuisine_filter

rules._comment: Client's protein-source list: at least one dish a day whose key_ingredient is one of these, anywhere across flavoured rice / veg gravy / veg dry / salad / dal. Selected on key_ingredient because that is how the client specified it. daily_min (not min) so it means 'every day' whatever the horizon length; it is capped per day to what that day can place, so a thin day relaxes instead of going INFEASIBLE. Variant spellings (channa_dal, gram_dal, cottage_cheese, soppu_moong, allesande, kofta_made_from_lentil) were folded into these canonical values by scripts/protein_key_ingredients.py. Not covered because Bangalore carries no such dish: soya chaap, moong chilla; pesarattu exists but is filed as bread, not one of the five slots.
rules.name: stryker_protein_source_daily

rules._comment: The protein must not always be the dal. At least 3 days a week carry one OUTSIDE the dal slot — the three ordinary (non-chinese, non-biryani) days. HARD, and `min` is auto-capped to the days that can actually place a match, so it degrades instead of going INFEASIBLE. The chinese and biryani days are pushed for by the companion soft rule rather than mandated here: every day can supply one today, but forcing all five would trade a whole plan for one dish the moment another rule disagrees.
rules.name: stryker_protein_outside_dal

rules._comment: 'these 2 days also can possibly have without breaking rules' — the chinese and biryani days. Soft twin of the floor above: one penalty per day with no non-dal protein, so the solver takes all five whenever nothing else has to give, and yields when something does. priority medium keeps it under the theme and high-tier rules.
rules.name: stryker_protein_outside_dal_all_days
